name: White supremacy
summary: White supremacy is the belief that white people are inherently superior to other races and should hold power, privilege and often separate territory. Its adherents draw on 19th and early 20th century race science, defend or seek segregation, exclusion of non-white immigrants and denial of equal political rights, and frequently adopt antisemitic conspiracy theories. Strands range from legal segregationists and slaveholder ideology to Nazi-style racial states, white nationalist ethnostate projects and violent militias.
scope: The mainstream of explicitly white-supremacist belief as documented in Wikipedia's account of the doctrine, with Madison Grant's The Passing of the Great Race and Alexander Stephens's Cornerstone Speech as primary expressions, plus white nationalist separatism. It does not cover the broader topic of racism or non-white supremacist movements, and economic and religious positions vary widely between strands.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Welfare provision is generally framed around the in-group and not a stated concern of the sources, so an adherent would likely oppose broad state benefits that also serve non-whites; inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Economic policy is secondary to race in the sources; wage floors are inferred to be opposed as part of the usual far-right economic outlook.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Strands split between market-friendly and anti-capitalist positions, as the sources centre on racial control of resources, not on markets.

public-ownership.rationale: Neo-Nazi strands favour state economic control while others favour private enterprise; the sources document no common line.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Some strands attack Jewish finance while others defend white property-holders; economic questions are not settled in the sources.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are not a topic of the sources; adherents are inferred to oppose them as multiracial or leftist bodies.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property was central to slaveholder defences of racial order, but modern strands are split on property rights; inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The sources do not address regulation; strands split between anti-corporate and pro-business views.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare is commonly framed as benefiting non-white groups, so many adherents favour cutting it; inferred, as the sources say little.

worker-ownership.rationale: No source supports collective ownership; it is inferred to be rejected as a left-wing programme.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Anti-government militias and distrust of the state suggest opposition to surveillance, though the sources do not state it.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the generally conservative and authoritarian social outlook of the movement.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents routinely oppose laws that would restrict racist speech; inferred from their position as its main targets.

strong-leader.rationale: Grant favoured rule by a picked minority and Nazism exalted a leader; inferred as the typical authoritarian lean.

state-harmful.rationale: Historic supremacists wanted the state to enforce racial hierarchy, though militias are hostile to government; most adherents are not anarchists.

limit-guns.rationale: Militia and armed-group culture in the movement suggests opposition to gun limits; inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: Segregationist states relied on police power while modern militias distrust the federal government, so strands split.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the rigid views on sexuality noted in the sources.

decide-locally.rationale: Segregation was defended via states' rights, but nationalist strands want central white-majority states; split.

rehabilitation.rationale: Grant's eugenics stresses inherited traits and removing defective lines over reform; inferred opposition.

traditional-family.rationale: Sources note rigid views on gender and sexuality in some groups and concern for white birth rates.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The sources note that white supremacist groups target LGBTQ+ people.

abortion-legal.rationale: Concern for white birth rates and Grant's pro-natal aims for desired groups point to opposition; inferred and not uniform.

more-religion-public.rationale: Christian Identity favours religious politics while Creativity is atheist and others are pagan; genuinely split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The doctrine rejects racial equality as a principle, so adherents reject redress for racial injustice.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the rigid view of sex and gender roles in some groups.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: White nationalists see white culture as foremost and Grant sought to preserve Nordic heritage.

gradual-change.rationale: Violent and revolutionary strands seek radical restructuring and Grant despaired of existing institutions; inferred.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration restriction is central: Grant, the 1790 and 1920s laws and white nationalist aims all stress it.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Conspiracy theories about global Jewish control and nationalism imply hostility to international bodies; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Nationalist economics is inferred; the sources do not address trade.

nation-first.rationale: Nationalist strands prioritise their own nation, though loyalty is to race across borders; inferred.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred from hostility to universalist human rights claims and non-white beneficiaries.

open-borders.rationale: Open borders contradict the central aim of preserving a white majority or homeland.

limit-growth.rationale: Grant was interested in conservation but strands disagree on growth; not a defining issue.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The sources do not address climate; inferred from the movement's general hostility to expert-led state action.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed; strands diverge on modernity.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; no common line among strands.

revolution-justified.rationale: Militia groups seek to overthrow the government and form a white homeland, though mainstream segregationists worked through the law.

experts-over-public.rationale: Grant held that a majority is inferior to a picked minority, though modern movements distrust expert elites; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Inferred opposition to socialist planning, though Nazism used heavy state direction.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred as a left-wing economic model the movement rejects.

land-value-tax.rationale: None of the sources address this issue, and strands of the movement differ; left neutral.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Grant favoured hereditary advantage and lines of good stock; inferred opposition to heavy inheritance taxes.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred from opposition to unconditional benefits that also reach non-whites.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic nationalism is a common lean; the sources do not state it.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Strands split between statist and market positions.

widespread-small-property.rationale: None of the sources address this issue, and strands of the movement differ; left neutral.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: No source supports abolishing money; it is a left-wing aim the movement rejects.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Creativity and other groups promote conspiracies about Jewish control of banks, suggesting hostility to central banking; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Nazi-influenced strands favoured it while others did not address it.

one-party-rule.rationale: Nazism and one-party Jim Crow South relied on it but other strands are indifferent.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Grant admired aristocracy, but strands lack a common view on monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: Non-whites were disenfranchised and Grant argued universal suffrage favours the average over the capable.

workers-councils.rationale: A left-wing form of rule the movement rejects.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred from Nazism, colonial dominance and the focus on racial power.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Segregation, subordination and violence against non-whites are central to the doctrine, so force is not restricted to defence.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Adherents would back banning opposing movements but not their own; the sources give no clear position, so this leans on inference.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Stephens and Grant accept subordination of a racial group as the legitimate basis of social order; inferred for domination.

vanguard-party.rationale: The doctrine is not framed around the working class or revolutionary parties; inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Grant's eugenics and elite rule treat the unfit as a burden, and welfare is framed around the in-group; inferred.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Inferred: public housing is not addressed, and strands range from welfare-minded to free-market.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred: the audit finds a lean against unions, so limits on strikes fit, though this is not a stated concern.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Inferred: the sources blame race, not population growth, and economic views vary by strand.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Grant treats race mixture as a reversion to the lower type, and white nationalists want racially homogeneous states.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Stephens and Grant rest government on racial hierarchy and elite rule, which a lottery among all citizens would undo.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred: authoritarian strands accept suspending protections against perceived enemies, while others emphasize constitutional rights.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not address price controls and economic positions vary widely between strands.

party-controls-media.rationale: Inferred: Nazi-style strands favor state control of information, while other strands rely on free speech claims.

party-commands-army.rationale: Inferred: Nazi-style strands put the army under the party, but segregationist and militia strands do not.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from its support for immigration limits: a long wait fits, though many adherents would deny non-white citizenship entirely.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Grant favours rule by a racial elite, and ordinary-wage office is not stated; inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Organised supremacist movements are hierarchical and demand loyalty to the cause; inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: White nationalism centres on ethnostates and national or racial separation, which cuts against binding supranational bodies; inferred.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Grant and authoritarian strands favour strong elite leadership over democratic legislatures; inferred.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Religion varies sharply between strands, from Christian Identity to paganism and atheism.

clerical-rule.rationale: Strands are split on religion and many are secular or pagan, so rule by religious scholars is not typical; inferred.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The ideology is racial-nationalist and puts loyalty to the white race and its state first; inferred.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Nazi-style and other supremacist strands censor culture deemed degenerate; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed; Grant distrusts democracy but no position on term limits is stated.

recall-officials.rationale: Grant criticises democratic rule and favours elite control, so recall by voters is inferred as disfavoured.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; strands differ on foreign alliances; neutral.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Inferred: property-owning in-group households are favored; no call to abolish renting.

people-in-arms.rationale: Inferred: militias and armed citizen groups are common in the movement.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Inferred: strands idealize the rural homestead and stock against multiracial cities.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split on reunifying nations; neutral.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred: the movement's populist rhetoric distrusts universities and educated elites.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Belief in the inherent superiority of white people directly denies the equality of cultures.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred: strands generally favor harsh punishment, historically including racialized capital punishment.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred: social conservatism and opposition to egalitarian curricula.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred: many strands, such as Christian Identity, are religiously fundamentalist.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred: social conservatism and moral purity themes in the movement.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: White nationalism defines the nation by white ancestry, so descent-based citizenship follows.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred: a white ethnostate would favor a single dominant language and culture.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Inferred: no concern for minority religions, and Jews and Muslims are targets.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred: the movement stresses conformity to in-group norms.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Wealth transfers to non-white countries run against a race-first outlook, and cancelling debts is not a stated concern; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The sources do not link independence to economic change, and strands differ on economics.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Grant distrusts democracy and favours rule by a racial elite, so a popularly elected assembly is unlikely to be favoured; inferred.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Grant's elite rule and segregationist states curbed political freedoms, so adherents would accept limits for a goal; inferred.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Duties are owed to the in-group race, and Grant opposes aid to inferior races; inferred from this.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: White nationalist and ethnostate projects favour strong sovereign defence; inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Grant doubts popular rule and favours elite selection, so a direct popular vote is unlikely to be favoured; inferred.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Antisemitic conspiracy theories about bankers are common, so independent bank power is likely to be distrusted; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Ethnostate projects hold the racial homeland as non-negotiable; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Economic views vary widely between strands and the sources give no answer.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred from solidarity among white nations; strands differ on alliances.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents are likely split on custody presumptions.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred: property is generally defended and redistribution is feared as benefiting non-whites.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Fascist strands are among the doctrine's historical forms; inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Nazi-style strands reject the equation while anti-communist strands might accept it; leans reject.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Modern adherents favor the Lost Cause view, though Stephens' Cornerstone Speech itself names slavery as the foundation.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Preserving Confederate and similar monuments is a common adherent cause; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Overlaps with online far-right gender politics; inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; strands differ on gender and family policy, so adherents split.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Grant argues that democratic institutions suit only certain races; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Authoritarian and militarist strands favor military intervention; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Pronatalist strands favor support for mothers, traditionalist strands oppose wages for housework; split.

filial-duty.rationale: Traditional family hierarchy is common in white-supremacist movements, but the sources do not address it; inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; Grant favoured an elite of the "best" stock while segregationists relied on white-only elections, so adherents split.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Nationalist strands guard national assets for the in-group, but the sources do not address foreign takeovers; inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Defence of traditional marriage suggests opposition to easy divorce, though the sources are silent; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Strands favour hierarchy and rule by the racial in-group, not instructed delegates; inferred from the doctrine's elitism.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not addressed; some strands favour private markets and others in-group welfare, so adherents split.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Private property in land, including for white settlers, is the usual assumption, though the sources are silent; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Not addressed; segregationist states had legislatures, but ethnostate and authoritarian strands do not require one; adherents split.

single-official-language.rationale: White nationalism seeks a culturally uniform homeland, so a single common language fits, though it is not a stated demand; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Ethnostate projects aim to keep land in the in-group's hands, but a ban on foreign owners is not stated; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Adherents deny that unequal racial outcomes show discrimination and attribute them to inherent racial differences, as Grant does.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; some strands decry consumer culture as Jewish-driven decadence while others do not; split.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Not addressed; militias and Nazi-style strands back armed action while segregationist strands never took a view; split.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Nazi-style racial states used force to bring neighbours into line, but the mainstream sources do not address it; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Economic positions vary sharply between strands, so adherents are split.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not addressed directly by the sources; inferred from white nationalist exclusion of outside influence.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: White nationalists fear demographic replacement and want higher white birth rates while ending non-white immigration.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed directly by the sources; inferred from ethnostate and separatist aims.

job-guarantee.rationale: Not addressed directly by the sources; inferred from a far-right opposition to broad state economic guarantees.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not addressed directly by the sources; inferred from Grant's and Stephens's rejection of equal political rights.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Not addressed directly by the sources; inferred from a hierarchical view of law and order.

non-intervention.rationale: Foreign policy varies between strands; adherents are split.

industrial-unions.rationale: Economic organisation varies sharply between strands.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The sources note that adherents frequently adopt antisemitic conspiracy theories.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage rules enforcing racial lines and reproduction mean legal marriage is wanted, not abolished.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Not addressed directly by the sources; inferred from a secretive, hierarchical outlook.

local-production.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents are indifferent.

informal-organisation.rationale: Not addressed directly by the sources; inferred from both leaderless-resistance cells and formal organisations existing in the milieu.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not addressed directly by the sources; inferred from a nationalist outlook hostile to international bodies.

religious-nation.rationale: Religion varies from Christian Identity to paganism to atheism, so adherents are split.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The ideology places one race on top but does not frame this as ritual tribute between states; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: No stated line on regional revenue; strands diverge between national and separatist projects.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The doctrine does not call for common ownership of productive property; inferred.

defeat-communism.rationale: Strands including Nazi-style racism cast communism as a Jewish conspiracy to be defeated; inferred as majority view.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: No stated position on how public services are delivered.

religion-illusion.rationale: Religion is often central, with strands such as Christian Identity, so it is not treated as a fading illusion; inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Strands split between pro-market and anti-capitalist views.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of equality and its view of the sexes and races as naturally ordered.

socialized-care.rationale: Strands stress the family and racial reproduction, so private care is preferred; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Some strands such as Nazi Germany purged foreign words, while others did not; adherents are split.

treaties-binding.rationale: Cornerstone-style ideology subordinates other races, and treaties with native peoples were broken; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: It seeks an ethnostate or racial order and not small communes with common property; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Colonialism and ethnostate projects have promoted settlement by the dominant race in minority areas; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Fascist and white nationalist strands often claim a third position beyond capitalism and communism; inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: White nationalist separatism claims ancestral homelands for white peoples; inferred from the ethnostate project.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Holocaust denial is common among neo-Nazi strands and antisemitic conspiracy theories, though segregationist strands do not share it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from the traditional-hierarchy and 'racial purity' outlook; the sources do not discuss sexuality.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Cornerstone Speech's order rests on denying equality to a subordinate race, so dissent against it was not tolerated; inferred for suppression of opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Religious positions vary widely between strands and most defend racial rather than religious orthodoxy; inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Colonial and slaveholder strands treated subject peoples as existing for the benefit of the dominant race.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: a duty on all believers to defend a Muslim land has no place in a doctrine centred on white racial interest.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: governing by religious law is not a central concern, and Islamic rule is opposed by most strands.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The doctrine denies equal political rights to non-whites, so broad direct participation is not a goal; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The doctrine denies that racial hierarchy is oppression and rejects the equality claims on which intersectional analysis rests.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist and biological-hierarchy outlook; the sources do not address it.

assisted-dying.rationale: Grant's eugenics favoured eliminating the 'unfit', but the sources say nothing on consensual assisted dying; adherents are split.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Some white nationalists claim to be beyond left and right, others align firmly with the right; inferred and split.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: Marxist concepts of alienation are foreign to a race-first doctrine.

islam-incompatible.rationale: White nationalism opposes non-white immigration on cultural and racial grounds; Islam is typically cast as alien. Inferred, sources do not discuss Islam directly.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Strands split between Christian Identity-style religious claims and secular race science.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred: many white nationalists favour a Western cultural identity for state institutions, but strands differ.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The doctrine is indifferent to employment-law questions; inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: Economic positions vary widely between strands, from slaveholder to corporatist views, as the scope notes.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred: separatist and militia strands treat strong force as needed to defend the race and its territory.

rich-first.rationale: The Cornerstone Speech's hierarchical social order accepts that some groups prosper ahead of others; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Strands differ between isolationist separatism and defence of a wider white or Western bloc; inferred.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Strands split between monarchist, elite-rule and republican forms, and the sources do not address hereditary office as such; inferred.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Antisemitic finance conspiracies are common but a user-owned banking model is not a stated concern; inferred and split.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Hostility to international finance and globalism is common in the conspiracy strands, so refusing IMF terms is likely welcomed; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: Grant favours rule by a racial and social elite over mass democracy, and segregationist regimes used property and tax tests to exclude voters; inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The doctrine rests on hierarchy and domination, so an adherent would reject the claim that these should be ended; inferred.

reification.rationale: A Marxist critique of capitalism is not part of the doctrine and is usually rejected; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Adherents more often blame Jewish or elite media control than wealth as such, and do not accept the equal-liberty framing; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Segregationists defended legal codes while Nazi-style strands ruled by decree, so adherents split; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: Stephens states that government rests on racial inequality, and white supremacy seeks power held by whites, with exclusion of others from political rights.

online-participation.rationale: Not addressed; the movement uses the internet heavily but has no settled view on online political decisions; inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents distrust governments but have no common view on open records; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The core concern is race mixing, not religion, and religious views vary widely between strands; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Boycotts of Jewish-owned shops are a familiar antisemitic tactic that many strands accept; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Grant favours rule by a racial and eugenic elite and the Cornerstone Speech rests on a hierarchy of rights, so adherents would distrust lot-chosen mass deliberation; inferred, not addressed.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Strands split between traditionalist Christian segregationists and movements such as Christian Identity that reinterpret scripture along racial lines; the sources do not address it.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Economic positions vary widely between strands, from slaveholder and capitalist views to Nazi-style anti-finance ones, so there is no common answer.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the movement's traditionalist and hierarchical view of society; the sources do not discuss military service.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Strands are religious or hostile to mainstream churches, but none documented here argue for state-promoted atheism; inferred.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred from Grant's rule by a racial elite and his stress on order and exclusion, which need coercive enforcement.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Stephens grounds government on the inequality of the races, so sharing executive power with other communities is rejected.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Strands differ on welfare, and the sources open say little on charity versus state aid.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred from Grant's elite-rule and anti-democratic stance; term limits are not discussed.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from Grant's scepticism of democracy and mass participation; delegable voting is not discussed.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Grant fears the extinction of the Nordic race, not of humanity, so a general priority on human extinction is not implied either way.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the hierarchical, traditionalist outlook of most strands; religion varies between them.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the patriarchal, traditionalist outlook documented for most strands; not directly stated.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred: white nationalist projects limit political rights to the in-group, so foreign residents would not vote.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred: the sources state no housing view; rents are left to owners in the usual adherent outlook.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: no stated view; adherents generally defend existing property rights.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: Nazi-style and militia strands organise uniformed youth and paramilitary groups for racial ends.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: The sources state no position on nuclear basing.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred: white nationalism stresses racial sovereignty and separate territory, which foreign bases would compromise.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred: adherents commonly deny or relativise genocide such as the Holocaust and resist official recognition.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Strands range from corporatist to capitalist; the sources state no position.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine glorifies force and does not condemn defensive killing.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred: Grant treats the white race as a continuous stock whose descent runs from its racial origins.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred: race doctrine rests on biological essentialism, extended to sex.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred: adherents hold fixed biological categories, including for sex.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred: Nazi-style and militia strands honour their dead as martyrs of the race.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred: several strands, such as Nazi mysticism and Christian Identity, frame politics as a struggle of good and evil races.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred: white nationalists seek an ethnostate gathering the race in one territory.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred: the ethnostate project puts racial separation and state power first.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred: adherents are mostly traditionalist about religious language.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred: adherents are traditionalist on gender roles and would not subject texts to this test.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The doctrine holds that white people should hold power and privilege and be preferred in economic and political life.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred: an ethnostate project implies one territorial unit for the white population.

independent-unions.rationale: Adherents vary and the sources do not discuss unions.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred: socialism is usually rejected as internationalist or Jewish-influenced.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Economic positions vary widely between strands.

second-chamber.rationale: Never addressed; structure of legislatures varies.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: most strands favour private property or racial states over community ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Adherents split between centralised racial states and states'-rights segregation; never addressed.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from the stress on the white family and its reproduction in Grant and in white nationalism.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred: open adherents face deplatforming and prosecution and so favour anonymity.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred: Grant and Stephens subordinate individuals to the race.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Strands range from Christian Identity to pagan and atheist; adherents are split.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred: Grant's account sees race degeneration in cities and immigrant concentrations.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The doctrine holds that whites are a group with interests to defend through organising, as the white nationalist strand states explicitly.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in white identity is central to the doctrine and to white nationalism.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Strands range from defensive segregationists to Nazi-style conquest; adherents are split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred from Grant's racial classification of Europeans, which treats race and not language as what defines a people.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine organizes politics by race and not by religious community.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Antisemitic and replacement conspiracy theories are common, and these describe hostile forces working to weaken the white nation; inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from the usual opposition to broad social programs that also serve non-whites.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental policy is not a concern of the sources; inferred as opposed under the usual far-right outlook.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from Grant's and the ethnostate strand's aim of preserving the white race for later generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's hierarchical and traditional views; the sources do not address it.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's militarist and violent strands; not stated in the sources.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from the conspiratorial strand, which distrusts open international institutions.

capital-controls.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; strands split between market and anti-capitalist positions.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Militias and armed in-group groups feature in the milieu, so adherents would resist disarmament while favouring the state's armed forces under white control; inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Adherents favour racial struggle and see the army as the nation's defender; inferred, with some strands opposing wars they call Jewish-driven.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Economic positions vary widely between strands, as the scope notes; no source states a position.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Welfare is framed around the in-group and adherents oppose benefits that also serve non-whites; inferred.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Economic positions vary widely between strands and the sources do not address fiscal rules.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine of white supremacy and colonial hierarchy: reshaping world rules to favour non-white developing countries is opposed.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Most strands want to capture the state or build an ethnostate, not abolish it; some militant strands want to overthrow it; inferred.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred: adherents seek a racially defined order and not open-ended economic experiments among communities.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents are split on environment and economy.

sacred-nation.rationale: White nationalism treats the nation or race as an enduring community whose preservation gives meaning, and Grant frames race as a lasting heritage to protect.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from hostility to benefits seen as favouring non-whites; the sources do not discuss it.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: adherents reject the framing of racial or regional exploitation by a dominant group and treat hierarchy as natural.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Grant and Stephens hold that races differ in kind and that equality is false, which rejects a shared nature grounding equal dignity and rights.

public-service-media.rationale: Adherents distrust mainstream media as hostile or controlled; state-funded independent media is not endorsed; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Exclusive racial and Christian-identity strands treat other religions as rivals, though the sources do not address it; inferred.

farm-price-support.rationale: Economic positions vary widely between strands, as the scope notes.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Strength and security of the in-group favour keeping deterrent arms; inferred, as the sources do not discuss it.

workers-own-party.rationale: Class parties cut across the racial in-group that adherents prioritise; inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: Adherents may split between condemning the practice as foreign and ignoring it; the sources do not address it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Patriarchal strands such as the Confederate worldview in the Cornerstone Speech favour male-led property and family; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; inferred as indifferent.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Strands vary widely on economic regulation and the sources do not discuss the question.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Chiefs would be rejected as non-white authority in most strands, though the sources do not address it; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The sources do not address ecology; some strands have an environmental blood-and-soil thread while others do not.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Harsh, fixed punishment is common in strands that stress order and racial hierarchy; inferred.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Exclusion of non-white immigrants is the stated aim, so a language path to settlement is rejected; inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Economic positions vary widely between strands and the sources do not address unions; inferred from that split.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's aim of excluding non-whites from political power, which favours tighter restrictions on who may vote.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Religious views range from Christian Identity to pagan and secular strands, so adherents split; inferred from the sources' note on religion.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Grant and other theorists distrust democratic majorities and want rule by a racial elite, so adherents would not call a government legitimate merely for holding fair elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on family and white birthrates; not directly addressed in the sources.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Not addressed; adherents favour state authority over non-whites but many rely on the internet to organise, so inferred as split.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from hostility to broad welfare that would also benefit non-whites.

women-suffrage.rationale: Historical segregationists were split, some backing women's votes to bolster the white electorate and others opposing them; inferred.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from traditionalist views of gender roles and, for many strands, a religious identity.

race-social-construct.rationale: The doctrine rests on race as a real biological hierarchy; Grant's text treats racial types as fixed hereditary groups.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from traditionalist gender views and hostility to state equality programmes.

missingStatements.text: Marriage and having children across racial lines should be discouraged.
missingStatements.rationale: Marriage outside the white race is usually rejected and Grant calls race crossing reversion to the lower type.

notes: Economic positions (market versus statist) and religion (Christian Identity, paganism, atheism) vary sharply between strands, so many answers on those topics are low confidence or neutral. Many answers rest on inference because the sources focus on race and not on policy.
